dicas.texto: Você está indo bem! Para transformar 20.000 em 100, precisamos reduzir o número. Que operação matemática usamos para diminuir um valor mantendo a proporção?
Tente dividir 20.000 por 100. O resultado dessa conta será o seu fator de escala para ambos os lados da razão.
Se você cortar dois zeros de 20.000, o que sobra? Esse é o número que você deve usar para dividir tanto o 20.000 quanto o 100.
Pense: 20.000 / X = 100. Se você simplificar os zeros, verá que X é 200. Use 200 como seu fator de escala!

interfaceCtat.descricao: Interface FIXA do tutor (a mesma tela para todos os problemas): enunciado com as partes da tarefa e, abaixo, uma TABELA de razões com três linhas — Total, Part 1 e Part 2 — e, em cada linha, quatro grupos de células: (1) a razão ORIGINAL (numerador e denominador, dois campos); (2) a coluna "Operation": dois seletores em que o aluno escolhe × ou ÷ (um para o numerador, um para o denominador); (3) a coluna "Scale Factor": dois campos com o fator aplicado ao numerador e ao denominador; (4) o RESULTADO: um campo para o numerador da razão equivalente, cujo denominador já vem impresso como 100 (isto é, a porcentagem), e um campo para o valor da porcentagem. Botão Hint; botão Done. Cada célula preenchida é um passo do aluno; a tabela inteira tem 24 células a completar.

dicas.texto: A defect rate compares the number of defective widgets with the total number made.
Use the total production as each denominator, then place the matching quantity above it.
The three rows use the totals 20000, 15, and 100 as their given quantities.
Fill the rows as total over total, 15 over total, and 100 over total.
The equivalent ratio must keep the same value while changing both terms in the same way.
Compare the original denominator with the target denominator and determine whether the size must decrease or increase.
The denominator changes from 20000 to 100, so the operation must make 20000 smaller.
Choose division and select the factor that makes 20000 equal to 100.
Both parts of a ratio must be divided by the same factor to preserve the comparison.
Divide the numerator 15 by the scale factor 200, just as the denominator was divided.
Since 15 is less than 200, the result must be a positive decimal smaller than 1.
Perform the final division of 15 by 200 and enter the resulting decimal in the percentage field.
Equivalent ratios are created by applying the same scale change to the numerator and denominator.
Find the operation that transforms the original denominator into the printed denominator of 100.
The denominator is reduced from 20000 to 100, which requires division by the same factor as in Part 1.
Select division and choose the factor that satisfies 20000 divided by the factor equals 100.
The numerator and denominator must be scaled equally so that the ratio remains equivalent.
Divide the Part 2 numerator 100 by the scale factor 200.
Dividing 100 by 200 produces a decimal between 0 and 1.
Complete the final division of 100 by 200 and enter that decimal in the Part 2 percentage field.
The total number of widgets represents the entire set, or one whole.
Scale the Total ratio to a denominator of 100 and check that both terms are transformed consistently.
The Total numerator and denominator are equal, so the percentage must represent the complete 100-part whole.
Enter the Total scale values and percentage, verify the three rows, and then activate Done to submit the table.

exercicio.statement:
A factory makes 20,000 widgets every week.

Part 1) If 15 of the widgets one week are defective, what is the rate of defects?

Part 2) If the next week 100 of the widgets are defective, what percentage of the widgets are defective? Part 1) If 15 of the widgets one week are defective, what is the rate of defects?
